name: Fast-Twitch Fiber Conversion
description: Converts a significant percentage of slow-twitch muscle fibers to fast-twitch Type IIx fibers, dramatically increasing explosive speed, reaction time, and sprint velocity at the cost of endurance. Users gain 40–80% improvement in burst speed and 20–30% improvement in reaction time. The modification makes the user startlingly fast in short bursts but exhausts them rapidly — a sprinter, not a marathon runner. The conversion affects all skeletal muscles, including those controlling eye movement and fine motor tasks, resulting in faster visual tracking and quicker hand-eye coordination. Zheng-Dao Bioelectric's version includes fatigue-buffer genes from hummingbirds that extend the duration of peak performance from seconds to minutes. The modification is popular among couriers, fighters, and anyone whose survival depends on being faster than the other person.
source_organism: Acinonyx jubatus (cheetah), Archilochus colubris (ruby-throated hummingbird, fatigue buffer)
procedure: Systemic retroviral injection targeting muscle fiber conversion, 3 sessions over 6 weeks
reversibility: Irreversible — fiber type conversion is permanent
side_effects: Dramatically reduced endurance — sustained effort becomes exhausting
Muscle tremors at rest from excess fast-twitch activity
Increased risk of muscle tears during explosive movement
Sleep disturbances from elevated baseline muscle tension
Heightened startle reflex — fast-twitch users flinch hard
social_perception: Respected in courier and combat circles. The 'cheetah look' — lean, twitchy, always slightly vibrating — is recognizable. Sprinter-gene users tend to be restless and fidgety, which reads as nervous energy to outsiders.
story_hooks: A courier with Cheetah Mod discovers they can outrun the automated pursuit drones in their district — until the drones receive a firmware update specifically targeting fast-twitch movement patterns
A fighter's fast-twitch conversion is so extreme that their startle reflex has become dangerous — they strike before conscious thought can intervene, and someone gets hurt
